title: Do EFkX allocations exist for a universal constant k?
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Is there a constant k such that every additive nonnegative goods instance, for any number of agents, has a complete allocation satisfying v_i(A_i)≥v_i(A_j without S) for every i,j and every S⊆A_j of size min(k, number of goods in A_j)?
context:
Approximate α-EFkX guarantees with α<1 and results for restricted additive valuations do not settle exact EFkX.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Asks whether a bounded additive relaxation suffices for fairness independently of the number of agents.
